# Canonical OpenQASM target first observations

`provenance.json` binds the unchanged 114-file prototype archive and its original
freeze record. The static reader checks safe regular-file members and all hashes
in memory. It never extracts archives or executes historical commands, paths,
Python drivers or Lean sources.

`reader-first-observation.json` separately retains the first current static
reader and its real failure: it associated the UTF-8 diagnostic with the wrong
historical attempt. The repaired reader checks the actual retained source and
diagnostic records. That harness failure is not target-checker evidence.
`native-first-observation.json` retains the first current comparison script,
target/request/packet and actual native refusal: the authored ideal omitted the
required null root-interface field. The checker correctly rejected that input;
the separate repair changes test data, not the acceptance contract.
`native-observer-first.json` preserves a later no-op mutation in the Python
observer: replacing a null interface with null correctly left a valid view
accepted. The corrected observer uses a different value. This harness error is
not a semantic counterexample or an acceptance-rule change.

`production-first.json` binds a separate focused 26-file archive: the first
three Lean sources, doubled-namespace import failure and mechanical repair;
the first seven Rust sources and successful compilation records; the Rust
null-to-null observer failure and a later test-spelling Clippy failure. Those
observer/lint repairs add no semantic rule. Successful current logs are not
duplicated, and archived driver commands are never run.

`compiled-audit-first.json` binds two further original records for the full
compiled-declaration audit's rejection of the generated private `word._unsafe_rec`
helper as partial. Its pre-fix source already resides unchanged in the production
first archive. A named theorem axiom audit had not detected that implementation
helper. The repair uses a standard bounded fold; fresh full audits/replay remain
separate validation, and the original failure is never reclassified as success.

Both first desired projects accidentally used an open `main`; their check and
export failures are retained. The separate public open functions subsequently
passed checking and refused closed export. Separate closed entries passed and
produced the actual one-qubit OpenQASM 3 target bytes. Source checks and numerical
observations do not prove source/export preservation.

The temporary study TP-31-TARGET-QASM-01 (P1) retains the first decoder,
mathematical, bounded-example and gate-phase failures, including the opaque
UTF-8 kernel-reduction obstruction. Repairs never overwrite those captures.
Its final exact byte decoder, explicit zero-width owner, complete instrument
bound and eight pre-observation gate matrices are bounded study evidence.
The manual H/readout ideal is labeled separately from source translation.

Fresh tests author new target bytes, original ideal graphs and requests for the
current native/CLI path. The canonical target is a closed terminal instrument
with an explicit consumed `Q<Unit>` input owner and one classical Bit result;
it is not an arbitrary-input pure map. Actual zero readout versus ideal H
readout has ordered Choi differences +1/2 and -1/2 and conservative bound one.
Its exact rational oracle is separate from floating simulation and Lean proof.

An engineering target comparison grants no exact source/export correspondence,
pure phase/control/inverse access, cleanup, resource certificate or constitutional
PR/RS admission, including epsilon zero. The preserved study adopts no new
target reference or guarantee and earns no Issue completion credit.
